Topic: Diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis, bootstrap inference, and SROC AUC comparison

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Research Question
How can we reliably compare the diagnostic accuracy of two tests when the same participants undergo both tests and only aggregated 2 × 2 tables are available?

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Motivation
When two diagnostic tests are evaluated on the same participants, their estimated sensitivities and false positive rates are correlated.
Existing bootstrap approaches may ignore this within-study dependence, which can underestimate uncertainty when comparing the AUCs of two SROC curves.
The main target is
\[
\Delta AUC = AUC_1 - AUC_2.
\]

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Main Idea
The paper proposes a correlation-aware bootstrap (CorrBoot) for inference on (AUC).
The method:

models the two diagnostic tests jointly using a four-variate random-effects model,
reconstructs feasible within-study correlations using Fréchet bounds,
stabilizes the correlation estimates using Fisher’s (z)-transformation,
generates bootstrap samples while preserving within-study dependence.

An important advantage is that the method does not require individual participant data.

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Simulation
The proposed CorrBoot method was compared with an independence-based bootstrap (IndepBoot).
The simulations varied:

the number of paired studies,
per-study sample size,
within-study correlation,
and the true difference in AUC.

CorrBoot generally maintained coverage close to the nominal 95% level, while IndepBoot showed undercoverage in several settings.

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Real-data Applications
The method was applied to three diagnostic meta-analysis datasets involving:

MRI criteria for nipple–areolar complex invasion,
ultrasonography versus MRI for placenta accreta spectrum disorders,
HCL versus MDQ for bipolar disorder screening.

In some comparisons, CorrBoot produced wider confidence intervals than IndepBoot, reflecting the additional uncertainty from within-study correlation.

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Main Takeaway
Ignoring correlation between diagnostic tests evaluated on the same participants can lead to overly optimistic inference.
CorrBoot provides a way to account for this dependence using only aggregated 2 × 2 data.

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
Limitations

The method relies on an approximate normal model on the logit scale.
Correlation estimation may be unstable when only a small number of paired studies are available.

title: A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-analysis
text:
My Notes
The key contribution of this paper is not a new AUC estimator itself, but a better way to quantify uncertainty in the difference between two SROC AUCs when diagnostic tests are correlated within studies.
The distinction between IndepBoot and CorrBoot is therefore mainly about whether the bootstrap preserves the dependence structure between the two tests.
